html:
North Macedonia is a landlocked Balkan country that left Yugoslavia in 1991. On this map, in 1994 and 2010, it appears under its earlier name, Macedonia. Its capital is Skopje.

It broke away peacefully after a referendum in 1991. Its name caused a long quarrel with Greece, whose northern region is also called Macedonia and which saw in the name a claim on the heritage of ancient Macedon and Alexander the Great. Because of that, it joined the United Nations in 1993 as "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia".

About a quarter of its people are Albanians. In 2001 an Albanian insurgency nearly became a civil war; the Ohrid Agreement ended it by giving Albanians more rights. In 2018 the Prespa Agreement with Greece settled the name dispute, and in 2019 the country became North Macedonia. It joined NATO in 2020.
